meaning: Identifier of this summarized verification check, retained for traceability within the assessment.
The type or named check summarized by this observation.
The business or person to which this check applies.
The recorded outcome of the check. Read the explanation and evidence; an unresolved result is not a successful verification.
The source or provider attributed to the check, when available and permitted to disclose.
When the verification observation was made, rather than when you retrieved it.
The readable explanation of the check's result and relevant limitations.
References to evidence supporting the checks in this section.
How the individual field was established, such as a declaration, source observation or document extraction. Different bases remain distinguishable.
The disclosure level applied to this identifier, such as masked or otherwise restricted presentation.
The kind of source supplying the verification evidence.
The type of verification check whose execution and result are recorded here.
The check's execution state, separate from the verification outcome. An uncompleted check cannot establish a successful result.
When the recorded human override decision was made.
Reference to the authorized actor responsible for the override, rather than an automatically inferred reviewer.
Whether the business observation is a candidate or a resolved legal-entity match under the stated evidence.
Industry classifications attributed to the business, retaining each classification scheme and evidence basis.
The classification system in which this industry code has meaning.
The industry code within the stated classification scheme.
The readable industry description associated with the code, when supplied.
The evidence basis for assigning this industry classification, distinguished from the business's own declaration.
The source's confidence measure for the industry assignment, retaining its own scale and meaning rather than becoming a credit score.
The supported assurance state for the person's identity. It does not establish creditworthiness or completion of unrelated checks.
The reported state of the entity's annual-return filing obligations, distinct from its registration status.
The annual-return years reported as outstanding by the source. Missing information does not establish that all years were filed.
The supported validation result for the address, rather than an assumption that a supplied address is verified.
Whether the linked party is represented as a person, business or other permitted entity type.
The evidence-supported verification state of the relationship, distinct from the identity verification of either party.
The type of ownership or control interest represented by this record, such as an economic, voting or other supported interest.
The method used to assess the identity document, retaining the source's stated basis.
The reported document-authenticity result. Unknown or unresolved authenticity does not establish a genuine document.
Source-reported document-quality measures with their own names and scales, rather than a combined credit or identity score.
Issuer attributed to the digital identity or wallet credential, when supported.
Country associated with the credential issuer as reported in the wallet evidence; it is not an inferred nationality.
When the wallet or credential verification was recorded.
The type of biometric check represented, such as liveness or face comparison; this does not expose a raw biometric template.
Identifier of the individual screening candidate hit.
The screening category to which the candidate hit belongs. A category alone does not establish a confirmed match.
Alternative names reported for the candidate hit, not automatically verified names of the assessed subject.
Permitted source reference for the screening candidate, when available. It does not grant access to a controlled report.
The source's similarity measure between the query and the candidate, retaining the original scale. Similarity is not a confirmed identity match.
A source-reported risk measure associated with the candidate hit, retaining its original method and scale. It is not an AMLOK default probability.
Additional allowlisted facts about the candidate, each retaining its own meaning and provenance.
The type of screening performed, which identifies the screening purpose separately from the datasets actually searched.
Execution state of the screening request. Incomplete execution does not establish a no-match result.
The screening outcome within the stated searched scope. A candidate, inconclusive result and completed no-match result have different meanings.
The tax identifier assessed, retaining its scheme, jurisdiction and disclosure restrictions.
The outcome of the stated tax-identifier or name check. It does not prove taxes were paid or that no tax debt exists.
The share classes reported for the entity, including supported rights, restrictions and nominal values.
The source-reported name of the share class.
The reported description of the share class and its provisions, when available.
The stated nominal or par value of the share class in its currency, rather than a market valuation.
The type of public or entitled record observation, which determines how its status and facts should be interpreted.
Whether and how the public-record subject has been matched to the assessed subject; a search candidate is not a resolved match.
Parties named in the record and their reported roles and supported links.
The party's name as recorded in the source record.
The party's reported role in the record, when supplied.
A supported link to an authorized business or person identity; null means no such link is established.
Reference to the party's associated address observation, when established.
Reported changes or filings that amend the original record.
The source reference identifying this amendment.
The source-reported type of amendment, when known.
The amendment's reported filing date, rather than the date it was collected.
Authorized document references supporting this amendment.
Dated events reported in the record's history, with their supporting document references.
The reported event date; null does not establish that the event did not occur.
The source-supported description of what occurred at this event.
Authorized documents supporting the reported event.
When the entitled consortium observation was reported, distinguished from account opening or closing dates.
The financial product type reported for the consortium observation.
The reported opening date of the observed product or account.
The reported closing date of the observed product or account, when known.
The source's reported reason for closure, without inferring default from closure alone.
Whether the source explicitly reports a first-payment default under its definition. Null is unknown, not false.
The original amount reported for the product or account, in the reported currency.
The amount the source reports as charged off, in its currency. It is not an estimate of future loss.
The type of online business presence observed, such as a website or other permitted business profile.
The supported match between the online presence and the assessed subject. A located page alone does not establish ownership.
The type of contact verification performed, distinguished from the value or verification result itself.
The reported assessment of possible document alteration. A signal requires interpretation and does not by itself prove fraud.
The outcome of the stated bank-account check, interpreted with its scope and ownership evidence. It does not establish financial capacity.
Recorded answers to the questionnaire, retaining question identity and answer provenance. A declaration is not automatically verified evidence.
The supported validation result for the recorded signature or signing evidence, rather than an inferred conclusion from a document's existence.
The result of comparing the stated fields across sources, preserving differences, missing values and unresolved comparisons.
A source-provided score with its name, scale, direction and method when known. It is not interchangeable with other provider scores or an AMLOK default probability.
The type of duplicate or related-identity check represented within the authorized scope.
Matches that may be disclosed within the authorized scope. This list does not expose identities from other customers or prove every possible match was searched.
The authorized matched business or person identity.
Reference to the associated authorized verification assessment, when available.
Source-reported similarity between the assessed identity and the authorized candidate, retaining its scale rather than implying a confirmed duplicate.
When this authorized match observation was recorded.
The recorded treatment or disposition of the match in the relevant list or review context, rather than an automatic adverse conclusion.
The AMLOK document identifier for the supporting file. Access is checked separately when the document is retrieved.
The type of supporting document represented by the reference.
The current permitted availability of the referenced document. A reference does not itself authorize download.
The verification source associated with the document reference.
Stable identifier of the normalized verification-assessment record, distinct from a provider's identifier.
The normalized resource discriminator identifying this record as a verification assessment.
The canonical business or person identity to which the normalized assessment applies.
Revision of the normalized record used to distinguish changes to the same logical observation.
When this normalized record was first created.
When this normalized record was last updated.
When the underlying verification observation was made, distinguished from ingestion or retrieval time.
The normalized schema version used to interpret this record.
The detailed verification assessment, including its checks, observations, coverage, provenance and limitations.
